title: P23 (HA/DR/upgrade rollback) current-truth closure
scopeSynthesisNote: The reconciled synthesis was handed to this writer by MASTER as the frozen scope for the package; its identifier is recorded here as evidence. Its concrete expression is the frozen test file below, which this writer did not author and did not edit.

frozenTestProvenance.authoredBy: the Claude test writer, re-issued on MASTER adjudication; this implementation writer neither authored nor edited either version
frozenTestProvenance.defect: The superseded frozen test's TABLE_NAME_HIDING guard recognised the Turkish hiding-claim only in its negative-verb shape (gostermiyor | gizliyor | sakliyor | aciklamiyor). Turkish also carries the same claim in the paired "ne ... ne de ..." frame, which negates a POSITIVE verb: "hata mesaji ne parolayi ne de eksik tablonun adini gosteriyor" asserts the hiding just as strongly while writing gosteriyor, not gostermiyor. The frozen P23C sentence uses exactly that second shape, so a negative-verb-only guard read it as honest.
frozenTestProvenance.consequence: Scenario P23D-5's read-back assertion - the one that proves this closure corrects a real frozen sentence rather than inventing a correction - could never match, so P23D-5 stayed RED on any tree regardless of what the five allowed files said, and the same blind spot would have let a genuine "ne ... ne de ..." overclaim through the projection deny-list unseen.
frozenTestProvenance.correction: The corrected frozen test adds a second alternative to TABLE_NAME_HIDING[2]: \bne\b(?=[^.]{0,120}\bne de\b)[^.]{0,120}tablo(?:nun)?\s+ad[\u0131i]n[\u0131i][^.]{0,60}(g[o\u00f6]steriyor|gizliyor|sakl[\u0131i]yor|a[c\u00e7][\u0131i]kl[\u0131i]yor), which requires the ne ... ne de frame by lookahead before accepting the positive verb. The negative-verb alternative is unchanged, so no previously-caught shape is lost.
frozenTestProvenance.verifiedOnThisTree: The superseded pattern returns false against planning/kernel-migration-rollback-p23c.json#userJourney.kullaniciYolculugu; the corrected pattern returns true against the identical byte-unchanged sentence. The corrected pattern still denies all five projections, so the guard was widened for the read-back and not weakened for the deny-list.
frozenTestProvenance.scopeUnchanged: The correction changes only how the frozen test recognises one Turkish negation shape. The counter, the capability delta, the readiness flags, the allowed-file set and the non-goals of this package are untouched by it.

QA1 itself did run the 16 Docker-dependent live suites as part of canonical `npm test`, preceded by one read-only `docker info` availability probe; both are recorded under qa.fullQaRun and neither is a package-created environment or a state-changing action of this package.
No registry push, no environment provisioning, no deployment, promotion, tag, release or production step.
No DAG edge, denominator, family grouping, package name or readiness flag is changed.
No P24 or P25 work is started, and no merged P23A/P23B/P23C artifact is edited.
AGENTS.md, RULES.md, versioning-policy.json, package.json and package-lock.json are untouched; no repo-root CLAUDE.md is created.

readinessClaim: Closing a package named HA/DR/upgrade rollback is neither high availability nor a disaster-recovery plan. Every stronger readiness flag stays false, no resilience flag is introduced true into currentTruth, and a hosted product remains not-runnable.

capabilityDelta.notRunnable: This truth-sync runs no drill, starts no container, provisions no environment, takes no backup, promotes no standby and migrates no schema; it only projects P23's already-merged P23A-P23C evidence into the roadmap counter, ROADMAP.md, README.md and CHANGELOG.md. Three proven drills on a single ephemeral host are not high availability, not a disaster-recovery plan, not point-in-time recovery and not a zero-downtime migration.

p23Evidence.substance: One verified owner-only custom-format backup, one total loss of the database container and its data volume, one restore into a fresh volume with the migration head, the four-table row truth, the two non-superuser roles, forced row-level security and the recomputable decision chain all back, and one further write chaining onto the pre-disaster genesis.

One real physical standby cloned with pg_basebackup under a replication-only role, sharing the primary's system identifier, streaming and refusing standby writes; the primary destroyed and its absence verified; the standby promoted by an operator and given the db alias so the never-restarted listener continues the same chain.

The repository's own locked alembic head revision run backwards to 0002_customer_records as the non-superuser migration role and re-applied, with the three earlier business tables surviving row-for-row, the never-restarted listener failing closed in between, and the decision history the rolled-back revision owned destroyed for good.

mergeOrderReadback: Each sub-package was cut from the commit the previous one merged as: P23B.base equals P23A.merge, P23C.base equals P23B.merge, and P23C.merge is the commit this counter is read as of. The order is checkable from the frozen records, not claimed.

subPackageFlagReadback.counterFrozenAt: All three merged manifests still record splitEvidence.counter = 22/25 and readinessFlags.p23Complete = false: none of them moved the counter, each left the closure to this package.

p23Residuals: All three drills are one manual, operator-driven run each on a single host inside the same self-deleting ephemeral environment; nothing detects a failure, nothing recovers on its own, nothing is monitored and Docker on that one machine is required.

P23A: no backup schedule, no retention policy, no offsite or second-machine copy, no WAL archiving and therefore no point-in-time recovery; no recovery objective (RPO or RTO) is agreed; the cluster-level roles return only because the restore re-creates them; verification reads run as the database superuser.

P23B: replication is asynchronous so unstreamed writes are lost on a real crash; there is no automatic failover, no synchronous replication, no zero-loss guarantee and no quorum, fencing or witness against split-brain; clients follow the promotion only because one container alias was moved by hand.

P23C: the rollback is a destructive maintenance-window outage, not a zero-downtime or online migration; no expand-and-contract or backward-compatible pattern exists, no data migration is attempted, and the re-upgrade brings the structure back and not one of those audit rows.

P23C: the refusal that maintenance window produces is the unchanged bridge's anonymous subprocess_failed 502 whose message is the runner's raw stderr, so PostgreSQL's own relation-does-not-exist text can reach the HTTP client; only the credential half of the owner-facing sentence is proven.
